## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step1_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS estimates, one row per 2010 CA tract.
- `../../../data/acs_step1_2024_tract.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates, one row per 2020 CA tract.
- Optional prior outputs in `../../../data/parity_reference` (§1.4) — separate
  schema and Southern California parity references for each product, including
  the product-specific filenames listed below.

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step2_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS tract measures (Southern California + Bay Area), with rental inventory (`rhu_inventoryE`), revised Step 1 pass-through columns, top-code/missing/zero flags, share, vacancy-rate, and CV measures.
- `../../../data/acs_step2_2024_tract.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS tract-source measures on `tr2020_id` (Southern California + Bay Area), with direct rental inventory, retained bedroom-rent pairs, top-code/missing/zero flags, structure, share, vacancy-rate, and CV measures.


This notebook:

1. Set up environment
2. Prepare 2012–2016 ACS tract measures
3. Prepare 2020–2024 ACS tract-source measures
4. Validate outputs

Either Step 2 notebook can run first. [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd) produces the
block-group aggregate; [02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd](02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd) produces both native tract tables.
Both use `step2_target_counties()` in `R/geography_qa.R` (§1.3).
`04_merge.Rmd` consumes all three unchanged products for its hierarchical panel
and source diagnostics. No inventory MOE or CV is introduced.

# 1. Set up environment

## 1.1 Load packages

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())

library(here)          # project-root-relative paths via here::here()
library(Hmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(assertr)
library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse)
library(spatstat)
library(matrixStats)   # weightedMean() for weighted aggregation
library(survey)        # core survey analysis functions
library(srvyr)         # tidyverse-style wrapper for survey
library(forcats)
```

## 1.2 Load helper functions

This stage's helpers — feather I/O, the merge/filter helpers, the weighting and
aggregation functions, flagging functions, and diagnostic helpers — live in
`R/assemble_helpers.R`. That file is self-contained for this notebook (it carries
its own `summ_var()`, distinct from the one used by `01_acs.Rmd`).
Shared geographic, key, schema, and parity diagnostics live in `R/geography_qa.R`.

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "assemble_helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "geography_qa.R"))
```

## 1.3 Set data directory and target counties

```{r set-paths}
# Trailing slash is intentional: save_data() builds paths with paste0().
data_dir <- "../../../data/"

county_config <- step2_target_counties()
southern_california_counties <- county_config$southern_california_counties
bay_area_counties <- county_config$bay_area_counties
target_counties <- county_config$target_counties

# Point to a preserved prior-output directory for repeatable analyst parity runs.
parity_reference_dir <- "../../../data/parity_reference"
```

## 1.4 Read prior outputs for parity checks

Prior outputs are read from `parity_reference_dir`, configured as
`../../../data/parity_reference`, before any output is saved. Preserve these
snapshots for repeated comparisons; saving candidates in `data_dir` does not
replace them. A missing reference is reported as **parity not checked**, never
as a pass. Reference and candidate must use the same statewide inputs and
measurement code, apart from the approved income correction and schema migration
below. Differences use a numeric tolerance of
`1e-10 * max(1, abs(prior), abs(candidate))`; shared column names, order, and
types must match exactly. Only `rhu_inventoryE` is joined from inventory
diagnostics into the Feathers.

### Decision: Permit only the agreed Step 2 schema migration

`compare_socal_parity()` remains strict by default (`schema_migration = NULL`).
This notebook opts into a fixed vintage-specific allowlist:

| `schema_migration` | Permitted additions | Permitted removals |
|---|---|---|
| `"2016"` | `vac_rentedE`, `vac_rentedM`, `rhu_inventoryE` | Estimate/MOE pairs for `rentmv1yr`, `rentmv5yr`, `rentyrblt`, `rentyrblt_14_16`, `rentyrblt_10_13`, `rentyrblt_00_09`, `rentyrblt_90_99`; `rhu_lrE`, `rhu_lr2E` |
| `"2024_tract"` | None | `rhu_lrE`, `rhu_lr2E` |

Native tract estimates and uncertainty remain unchanged. Retired fields are
rejected even when no parity reference exists.

Actual additions/removals appear in `schema_changes`; unlisted differences fail.
All shared columns retain the existing value, type, and order comparisons,
including the income and geographic classifications below. Inventory is validated
independently before saving and after reloading (§4.6), even when no reference
contains it. Save/reload schema comparison remains strict for every column.

### Decision: Verify the approved income correction against preserved references

The geographic parity check compares every shared output column. Only a changed
`med_hhincE` or `med_hhincCV` cell whose reference **and** candidate values match
the legacy and corrected expectations qualifies as `verified_income_correction`.
Expectations use 2016 inputs before censoring (§2.2), with the former
missing/top-coded-rent income exclusion applied only to the legacy estimate.
Both expected CVs use the reference `med_hhincM` and the existing
`(med_hhincM / 1.645) / med_hhincE` formula. Candidate MOEs remain subject to
ordinary parity. Missing values and numeric tolerance follow the same comparison
rule as all other columns. Without expectations, the helper remains strict.

### Decision: Keep source-specific references and preserve historical snapshots

The explicit map below retains the historical `acs_step2_16.feather` reference for the 2016
product. It does not rename or overwrite those snapshots. The new
2024 tract product uses only its own optional reference, keyed by `tr2020_id`;
only the two low-rent column removals are allowed by `schema_migration = "2024_tract"`.
Its shared schema and values remain strict, without income-correction or
allocation-boundary exceptions. An absent reference
leaves parity unchecked. Pre-censoring tract income is validated independently
in §3.4 even when no reference exists.

```{r load-parity-references}
parity_reference_files <- c(
  "16" = "acs_step2_16.feather",
  "2024_tract" = "acs_step2_2024_tract.feather"
)
prior_outputs <- read_step2_parity_references(parity_reference_dir, parity_reference_files)
```

# 2. Prepare 2012–2016 ACS tract measures

## 2.1 Load and restrict to the target counties

```{r load-restrict-16}
# Load 2016 ACS tract data
acs_16 <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step1_2016_tract.feather") |>
  select(-any_of(step2_cleanup_columns("2016")))
report_n(acs_16, "2016 ACS tracts loaded")
assert_unique_key(acs_16, "tr2010_id", "Statewide 2016 ACS")

## Use the same destination county set as the 2024 allocation.
n_before <- nrow(acs_16)
acs_16 <- select_target_counties(acs_16, tr2010_id, target_counties)
report_drop(acs_16, n_before, "tracts outside the target counties")
target_tract_ids_16 <- acs_16$tr2010_id
rent_raw_qa_16 <- acs_16 |>
  group_by(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5)) |>
  summarise(tracts = n(), raw_missing_rent = sum(is.na(rentE)),
            topcoded_rent = sum(rentE >= 3500, na.rm = TRUE),
            raw_missing_share = mean(is.na(rentE)),
            topcoded_share = sum(rentE >= 3500, na.rm = TRUE) / n(), .groups = "drop")

# Check % missing

check_vars <- c("rhuE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(check_vars, ~summ_var(acs_16, .x))
out
```

## 2.2 Flag and censor top-coded, missing, and zero values

### Decision: Flag then censor top-coded, missing, and zero values

For the 2016 tract data we record data-quality flags before censoring so the
information is preserved on the output:

- **Top-coded** (`tc_flag_*`): rent / `lqcrent` `>= 3500`, median value `>= 2,000,000`.
- **Missing** (`m_flag_*`): `NA` on the listed estimates.
- **Zero** (`zero_flag_*`): zero renter-occupied units / cash-rent units / median value.

Top-coded rent is then censored to `NA` (as in [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.4](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd)). The missing-rent rate is
interpreted alongside `zero_flag_rhu`: tracts with no renter-occupied housing
units have no occupied-renter rent to measure. They may still have positive
vacant rental inventory; inventory completeness is checked separately.

The income-retention decision in [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.4](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd) applies directly to each 2016 tract:
`med_hhincE` retains its source value or missingness regardless of rent censoring.
There is no intervening income aggregation for this vintage. `med_hhincCV` uses
the retained income estimate in its existing formula; see the
[income-censoring decision and validation](notes/income_censoring.md).

Capture the source income before censoring for the corrected expectation, and
apply the former rent exclusion only to the legacy expectation. As in [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.4](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd),
the reference-MOE join must preserve one row per destination tract. These
expectations validate income and CV changes without altering output columns.

```{r income-expectations-16}
expected_income_16 <- NULL
if (!is.null(prior_outputs[["16"]])) {
  expected_income_16 <- acs_16 |>
    transmute(
      tr2010_id,
      legacy_med_hhincE = if_else(is.na(rentE) | rentE >= 3500, NA_real_, med_hhincE),
      corrected_med_hhincE = med_hhincE
    ) |>
    left_join(select(prior_outputs[["16"]], tr2010_id, med_hhincM),
              by = "tr2010_id", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
    transmute(
      tr2010_id, legacy_med_hhincE, corrected_med_hhincE,
      legacy_med_hhincCV = (med_hhincM / 1.645) / legacy_med_hhincE,
      corrected_med_hhincCV = (med_hhincM / 1.645) / corrected_med_hhincE
    )
  assert_tract_keys(expected_income_16, target_tract_ids_16, "2016 income expectations")
}
```

```{r flag-censor-16}
# Flag top-coded values
tc_vars <- c("rentE", "lqcrentE", "med_hvalE")
acs_16 <- flag_tc_vars(acs_16, tc_vars)

# how many tracts have top_coded rent
table(acs_16$tc_flag_rent, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_16$tc_flag_lqcrent, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_16$tc_flag_med_hval, useNA = "ifany")


# Censor top-coded
summary(acs_16$rentE)
acs_16 <- censor_tc_vars(acs_16)
summary(acs_16$rentE)

# Flag missing values
missing_vars <- c("rentE", "lqcrentE", "rhuE", "rhucashE", "med_hvalE")
acs_16 <- flag_missing_vars(acs_16, missing_vars)

# Print summary of missing values
check_missing_vars(acs_16, missing_vars)

# Flag zero values
zero_vars <- c("rhuE", "rhucashE", "med_hvalE")
acs_16 <- flag_zero_vars(acs_16, zero_vars)
table(acs_16$zero_flag_rhu, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_16$zero_flag_med_hval, useNA = "ifany")

# How many tract groups missing rent have no renter-occupied housing units?
table(acs_16$m_flag_rent)
table(acs_16$m_flag_rent, acs_16$zero_flag_rhu) # 60% of tracts missing rent (42 of 70) have no renter-occupied housing units, so real missing rate is .7%, vs. earlier 1.7%
```

## 2.3 Build structure-type, percentage, CV, and rental-inventory measures

### Decision: Same vacancy / non-single-family measures as the 2024 block-group path

`mf5E`, `nsfaE`, `pctrvacE`, and `pctsvacE` are built here with the same
definitions used for the 2024 block-group product ([02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.6](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd)). For the
2016 tract data the source counts (`vac_forrentE`, `vac_forsaleE`, `ohuE`,
`rhuE`) are already present on the tract table, so no extra aggregation is needed.

```{r structure-pct-cv-16}
# Sum multifamily categories (mf5E = 5+ units; renamed from mfE so the cutoff is
# explicit and consistent with the 2024 output)
acs_16 <- acs_16 |>
    mutate(mf5E = mf_5_9E + mf_10_19E + mf_20_49E + mf_50E,
           smfE = sfd_attE + duplexE + quadplexE
    )

summary(acs_16$mf5E)
summary(acs_16$smfE)
summary(acs_16$sfd_detE)
# summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$huE)

# Calculate % vars
acs_16 <- calc_pct_vars(acs_16)

# Calculate MOE, CV
acs_16 <- calc_cv(acs_16)

# Non-single-family-attached count and rental / for-sale vacancy rates
# (defined as in 02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd, §2.6)
acs_16 <- acs_16 |>
  mutate(
    nsfaE    = smfE + mf5E,
    pctrvacE = if_else((rhuE + vac_forrentE) > 0,
                       vac_forrentE / (rhuE + vac_forrentE), NA_real_),
    pctsvacE = if_else((ohuE + vac_forsaleE) > 0,
                       vac_forsaleE / (ohuE + vac_forsaleE), NA_real_)
  )

# Check new vacancy-rate / structure measures (rates expected within [0, 1])
map_dfr(c("pctrvacE", "pctsvacE", "nsfaE", "mf5E"), ~summ_var(acs_16, .x))
```

### Decision: Sum the three 2016 tract inventory components directly

The source already has one row per 2010 tract. Use unit weights to compute
`rhu_inventoryE = rhuE + vac_forrentE + vac_rentedE`. Any missing required
estimate produces `NA`; missing MOEs, rent, or income have no effect. Retain
the Step 1 pass-through columns, including `vac_rentedE/M`, and join only the
inventory estimate from the separate diagnostics. No inventory MOE/CV is added.

```{r rental-inventory-16}
inventory_16 <- calc_rental_inventory(acs_16, tr2010_id)
assert_tract_keys(inventory_16, acs_16$tr2010_id, "2016 inventory diagnostics")
inventory_missing_sources_16 <- acs_16 |>
  select(tr2010_id, rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE) |>
  pivot_longer(c(rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE),
               names_to = "missing_component", values_to = "estimate") |>
  filter(is.na(estimate))
print(inventory_missing_sources_16, n = Inf, width = Inf)
inventory_county_qa_16 <- inventory_16 |>
  dplyr::count(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5), inventory_incomplete,
        zero_contributors = n_contributing == 0, name = "tracts")
print(inventory_county_qa_16, n = Inf)

before_inventory_join <- acs_16
acs_16 <- left_join(
  acs_16, select(inventory_16, tr2010_id, rhu_inventoryE),
  by = "tr2010_id", relationship = "one-to-one"
)
report_n(acs_16, "2016 inventory join (expected unchanged tract count)")
stopifnot("Inventory join must preserve every existing 2016 column and row" =
            identical(acs_16[names(before_inventory_join)], before_inventory_join))
rm(before_inventory_join)
assert_rental_inventory(acs_16, inventory_16, "2016 inventory after join")
inventory_reconciliation_16 <- reconcile_rental_inventory(acs_16, inventory_16, tr2010_id)
print(inventory_reconciliation_16, width = Inf)
```

## 2.4 Save 2012–2016 tract output

**Output:** `acs_step2_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS tract measures (Southern California + Bay Area),
including `rhu_inventoryE` and the revised Step 1 pass-through columns. It
replaces the production filename `acs_step2_16.feather`; the legacy file is
retained. `04_merge.Rmd` consumes this filename for its canonical baseline and
separate inventory diagnostics.

All previously included Southern California 2016 records must retain parity
on shared columns except individually verified income/CV corrections from §2.2.
Only the additions/removals listed in §1.4 are permitted under
`schema_migration = "2016"`, with actual changes in `schema_changes`. Validate
inventory independently against its source-component diagnostics before writing.
The complete
differences remain visible in `socal_parity_16`, using the same classifications
as [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.8](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd). Unexplained income changes, other column changes, and membership changes
fail; this vintage has no allocation-boundary exception.

```{r acceptance-16}
assert_tract_keys(acs_16, target_tract_ids_16, "2016 assembled tracts")
report_tract_counties(acs_16, target_counties, "2016 destination counties")
assert_rental_inventory(acs_16, inventory_16, "2016 inventory before save")
socal_parity_16 <- compare_socal_parity(
  acs_16, prior_outputs[["16"]], southern_california_counties,
  expected_income = expected_income_16, schema_migration = "2016"
)
```

```{r save-16}
report_n(acs_16, "2016 tract measures to save")

# # Save file
cat("Writing/replacing", file.path(data_dir, "acs_step2_2016_tract.feather"), "\n")
save_data(acs_16, data_dir, "acs_step2_2016_tract.feather")
```

```{r compare-medhhinc}
summary(acs_16$med_hhincE)
```

# 3. Prepare 2020–2024 ACS tract-source measures

## 3.1 Load and restrict to the target counties

### Decision: Retain the source's 2020 tract geography

`acs_step1_2024_tract.feather` is keyed by `tr2020_id`, as documented in the
[upstream schema](schemas/acs_step1_2024_tract.md). Select the same configured
counties as the other products, preserving one row per source tract. There is
no crosswalk or allocation in this path. Native dollar estimates, their MOEs,
and the retained bedroom-rent pairs carry through from Step 1.

```{r load-restrict-2024-tract}
acs_2024_tract <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step1_2024_tract.feather") |>
  select(-any_of(step2_cleanup_columns("2016")))
report_n(acs_2024_tract, "2024 tract-source ACS tracts loaded")
assert_unique_key(acs_2024_tract, "tr2020_id", "Statewide 2024 ACS tracts")
tract_fields_2024_tract <- c(
  "rent1bdrE", "rent1bdrM", "rent2bdrE", "rent2bdrM", "rent3bdrE", "rent3bdrM",
  "vac_rentedE", "vac_rentedM", "rent_id"
)
stopifnot("2024 tract-source input must retain its documented tract fields" =
            all(tract_fields_2024_tract %in% names(acs_2024_tract)))
stopifnot("2024 tract-source keys must be character California tract GEOIDs" =
            is.character(acs_2024_tract$tr2020_id) &&
            all(grepl("^06[0-9]{9}$", acs_2024_tract$tr2020_id)))

n_before_2024_tract <- nrow(acs_2024_tract)
acs_2024_tract <- select_target_counties(acs_2024_tract, tr2020_id, target_counties)
report_drop(acs_2024_tract, n_before_2024_tract, "2024 source tracts outside the target counties")
target_tract_ids_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract$tr2020_id
rent_raw_qa_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract |>
  group_by(county = substr(tr2020_id, 3, 5)) |>
  summarise(tracts = n(), raw_missing_rent = sum(is.na(rentE)),
            topcoded_rent = sum(rentE >= 3500, na.rm = TRUE),
            raw_missing_share = mean(is.na(rentE)),
            topcoded_share = sum(rentE >= 3500, na.rm = TRUE) / n(), .groups = "drop")
map_dfr(c("rhuE", "rentE"), ~summ_var(acs_2024_tract, .x))
```

## 3.2 Flag and censor top-coded, missing, and zero values

### Decision: Apply the established tract flags and retain source income

Use the existing tract flag lists and 2024 thresholds from [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd §2.4](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd): flag rent and
lower-quartile rent at `>= 3500`, and median house value at `>= 2000000`.
Capture top-code flags before censoring rent/lower-quartile rent to `NA`, then
construct the missing and zero flags as in §2.2. House value receives its flag
without censoring its estimate; bedroom-rent pairs remain unchanged.

Household income retains its source estimate, MOE, and missingness independently
of rent censoring. Preserve those inputs for the direct income/CV checks in
§3.4. This new product has no historical rent-dependent income correction to
permit in parity; any future reference comparison uses strict equality within
the existing numeric tolerance.

```{r income-source-2024-tract}
source_income_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract |>
  select(tr2020_id, med_hhincE, med_hhincM)
assert_tract_keys(source_income_2024_tract, target_tract_ids_2024_tract,
                  "2024 tract-source income inputs", key = "tr2020_id")
```

```{r flag-censor-2024-tract}
tc_vars_2024_tract <- c("rentE", "lqcrentE", "med_hvalE")
acs_2024_tract <- flag_tc_vars(acs_2024_tract, tc_vars_2024_tract)
table(acs_2024_tract$tc_flag_rent, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_2024_tract$tc_flag_lqcrent, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_2024_tract$tc_flag_med_hval, useNA = "ifany")

summary(acs_2024_tract$rentE)
acs_2024_tract <- censor_tc_vars(acs_2024_tract)
summary(acs_2024_tract$rentE)

missing_vars_2024_tract <- c("rentE", "lqcrentE", "rhuE", "rhucashE", "med_hvalE")
acs_2024_tract <- flag_missing_vars(acs_2024_tract, missing_vars_2024_tract)
check_missing_vars(acs_2024_tract, missing_vars_2024_tract)

zero_vars_2024_tract <- c("rhuE", "rhucashE", "med_hvalE")
acs_2024_tract <- flag_zero_vars(acs_2024_tract, zero_vars_2024_tract)
table(acs_2024_tract$zero_flag_rhu, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_2024_tract$zero_flag_med_hval, useNA = "ifany")
table(acs_2024_tract$m_flag_rent, acs_2024_tract$zero_flag_rhu, useNA = "ifany")
```

## 3.3 Build structure-type, percentage, CV, and rental-inventory measures

### Decision: Apply the existing tract-derived measure definitions

Build `mf5E`, `smfE`, `nsfaE`, the percentage measures, and existing MOEs/CVs
as in §2.3. Rental and for-sale vacancy rates use the same occupied-plus-vacant
denominators and remain missing when their denominators are non-positive.
The direct tract path does not construct block-group missing-rent shares or
interpolated rent.

```{r structure-pct-cv-2024-tract}
acs_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract |>
  mutate(mf5E = mf_5_9E + mf_10_19E + mf_20_49E + mf_50E,
         smfE = sfd_attE + duplexE + quadplexE)
acs_2024_tract <- calc_pct_vars(acs_2024_tract)
acs_2024_tract <- calc_cv(acs_2024_tract)
acs_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract |>
  mutate(
    nsfaE = smfE + mf5E,
    pctrvacE = if_else((rhuE + vac_forrentE) > 0,
                       vac_forrentE / (rhuE + vac_forrentE), NA_real_),
    pctsvacE = if_else((ohuE + vac_forsaleE) > 0,
                       vac_forsaleE / (ohuE + vac_forsaleE), NA_real_)
  )
map_dfr(c("pctrvacE", "pctsvacE", "nsfaE", "mf5E"), ~summ_var(acs_2024_tract, .x))
```

### Decision: Sum the three 2024 tract inventory components directly

Each unique 2020 tract contributes its own three estimates with unit weight:
`rhu_inventoryE = rhuE + vac_forrentE + vac_rentedE`. Any required estimate
missing as `NA` or `NaN` makes inventory `NA`; missing MOEs, rent, or income do
not. The existing helper validates source types, keys, and observed counts.
Component totals and completeness flags stay in the diagnostic table; join only
the inventory estimate onto the output, without changing its other columns.

```{r rental-inventory-2024-tract}
inventory_2024_tract <- calc_rental_inventory(acs_2024_tract, tr2020_id)
assert_tract_keys(inventory_2024_tract, target_tract_ids_2024_tract,
                  "2024 tract-source inventory diagnostics", key = "tr2020_id")
inventory_missing_sources_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract |>
  select(tr2020_id, rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE) |>
  pivot_longer(c(rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE),
               names_to = "missing_component", values_to = "estimate") |>
  filter(is.na(estimate))
print(inventory_missing_sources_2024_tract, n = Inf, width = Inf)
inventory_county_qa_2024_tract <- inventory_2024_tract |>
  dplyr::count(county = substr(tr2020_id, 3, 5), inventory_incomplete,
               zero_contributors = n_contributing == 0, name = "tracts")
print(inventory_county_qa_2024_tract, n = Inf)

before_inventory_join_2024_tract <- acs_2024_tract
acs_2024_tract <- left_join(
  acs_2024_tract, select(inventory_2024_tract, tr2020_id, rhu_inventoryE),
  by = "tr2020_id", relationship = "one-to-one"
)
report_n(acs_2024_tract, "2024 tract-source inventory join (expected unchanged tract count)")
stopifnot("Inventory join must preserve every existing 2024 tract-source column and row" =
            identical(acs_2024_tract[names(before_inventory_join_2024_tract)],
                      before_inventory_join_2024_tract))
rm(before_inventory_join_2024_tract)
assert_rental_inventory(acs_2024_tract, inventory_2024_tract,
                        "2024 tract-source inventory after join", key = "tr2020_id")
inventory_reconciliation_2024_tract <- reconcile_rental_inventory(
  acs_2024_tract, inventory_2024_tract, tr2020_id
)
print(inventory_reconciliation_2024_tract, width = Inf)
```

## 3.4 Validate and save 2020–2024 tract-source output

**Output:** `acs_step2_2024_tract.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS measures on native
2020 tracts in the target counties. See the
[output schema](schemas/acs_step2_2024_tract.md). Validate key membership,
county coverage, direct income retention, inventory, and the optional
source-specific parity reference before writing. These checks do not compare
this product with the block-group-aggregated product or the 2016 tracts.

```{r acceptance-2024-tract}
assert_tract_keys(acs_2024_tract, target_tract_ids_2024_tract,
                  "2024 tract-source assembled tracts", key = "tr2020_id")
report_tract_counties(acs_2024_tract, target_counties,
                      "2024 tract-source counties", key = "tr2020_id")
stopifnot("2024 tract-source income inputs must survive rent censoring unchanged" = identical(
  select(acs_2024_tract, all_of(names(source_income_2024_tract))), source_income_2024_tract
), "2024 tract-source income CV must use retained source income" = isTRUE(all.equal(
  acs_2024_tract$med_hhincCV,
  (source_income_2024_tract$med_hhincM / 1.645) / source_income_2024_tract$med_hhincE,
  tolerance = 1e-10
)))
assert_rental_inventory(acs_2024_tract, inventory_2024_tract,
                        "2024 tract-source inventory before save", key = "tr2020_id")
socal_parity_2024_tract <- compare_socal_parity(
  acs_2024_tract, prior_outputs[["2024_tract"]], southern_california_counties,
  key = "tr2020_id", schema_migration = "2024_tract"
)
```

```{r save-2024-tract}
report_n(acs_2024_tract, "2024 tract-source measures to save")
cat("Writing/replacing", file.path(data_dir, "acs_step2_2024_tract.feather"), "\n")
save_data(acs_2024_tract, data_dir, "acs_step2_2024_tract.feather")
```

# 4. Validate outputs

Re-loads the two saved native tract outputs separately and checks key uniqueness, missingness on
critical variables, the encoding of the flag columns, and the distribution of
every numeric column. Inventory completeness and reconciliation repeat the
pre-save checks using the saved estimates and separate source diagnostics.

```{r reload-step2}
acs16_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step2_2016_tract.feather"))
acs_2024_tract_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step2_2024_tract.feather"))
```

## 4.1 Check key uniqueness and duplicates

Expected: 2016 tracts are unique on `tr2010_id`; 2024 tracts are unique on
`tr2020_id`. Each retains its input-derived target membership.

```{r validate-keys-step2}
cat("acs_step2_2016_tract:", nrow(acs16_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs16_out$tr2010_id), "unique tr2010_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs16_out$tr2010_id)), "duplicate ids\n")
assert_tract_keys(acs16_out, target_tract_ids_16, "Saved 2016 tract keys")
assert_same_schema(acs16_out, acs_16, "Saved 2016 schema")
assert_tract_keys(acs_2024_tract_out, target_tract_ids_2024_tract,
                  "Saved 2024 tract-source keys", key = "tr2020_id")
assert_same_schema(acs_2024_tract_out, acs_2024_tract, "Saved 2024 tract-source schema")
assert_step2_cleanup(acs16_out, "2016")
assert_step2_cleanup(acs_2024_tract_out, "2024_tract")
```

## 4.2 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing geographic keys. Native `rentE` reflects censored top-codes
and tracts without cash-renting units; report counts without imposing a threshold.

```{r validate-missingness-step2}
cat("acs_step2_2016_tract missing tr2010_id:", sum(is.na(acs16_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2016_tract missing rentE:    ", sum(is.na(acs16_out$rentE)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2024_tract missing tr2020_id:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_tract_out$tr2020_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2024_tract missing rentE:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_tract_out$rentE)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2024_tract missing med_hhincE:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_tract_out$med_hhincE)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2024_tract missing rhu_inventoryE:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_tract_out$rhu_inventoryE)), "\n")
```

## 4.3 Check flag-variable encoding

The data-quality flags (`m_flag_*`, `zero_flag_*`, `tc_flag_*`) use numeric 0/1
values. The existing helpers store these as doubles; top-code and zero flags
retain `NA` when their source estimate is missing, while missing flags are
always observed. Geographic keys remain character and join indicators retain
their existing string/logical encodings.

```{r validate-flags-step2}
flag_cols_16 <- grep("^(m_flag_|zero_flag_|tc_flag_)", names(acs16_out), value = TRUE)
for (f in flag_cols_16) {
  cat("acs_step2_2016_tract", f, "-> class:", class(acs16_out[[f]]),
      "| values:", paste(sort(unique(acs16_out[[f]])), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
flag_cols_2024_tract <- grep("^(m_flag_|zero_flag_|tc_flag_)", names(acs_2024_tract_out), value = TRUE)
for (f in flag_cols_2024_tract) {
  values <- acs_2024_tract_out[[f]]
  cat("acs_step2_2024_tract", f, "-> class:", class(values),
      "| values:", paste(sort(unique(values), na.last = TRUE), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  stopifnot("2024 tract-source flags must be numeric 0/1 or missing" =
              is.numeric(values) && all(is.na(values) | values %in% c(0, 1)))
  if (startsWith(f, "m_flag_")) stopifnot(!anyNA(values))
}
stopifnot("2024 tract-source rent_id must remain logical TRUE" =
            is.logical(acs_2024_tract_out$rent_id) &&
            !anyNA(acs_2024_tract_out$rent_id) && all(acs_2024_tract_out$rent_id))
```

## 4.4 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in each output. Watch for impossible
values (negative counts, shares outside [0, 1], or rents far outside plausible
ranges).

```{r validate-numeric-step2}
print_numeric_summary(acs16_out, "acs_step2_2016_tract")
print_numeric_summary(acs_2024_tract_out, "acs_step2_2024_tract")
for (column in c("pctrvacE", "pctsvacE")) {
  values <- acs_2024_tract_out[[column]]
  stopifnot("2024 tract-source vacancy rates must be missing or finite fractions" =
              all(is.na(values) | (is.finite(values) & values >= 0 & values <= 1)))
}
```

## 4.5 Check county coverage and missing/top-coded rent

Both outputs must contain every configured county and no other county.
The raw diagnostics count tracts; final native-rent missing counts include
censored top-codes. Review county differences without imposing an empirical
missingness threshold. Income is retained independently of rent censoring; compare restored
income values and downstream measures using the
[income acceptance checks](notes/income_censoring.md#analyst-run-acceptance-checks).
The existing income-MOE behavior is preserved; its research ambiguity remains a
separate decision.

```{r validate-county-rent-step2}
report_tract_counties(acs16_out, target_counties, "Saved 2016 counties")
report_tract_counties(acs_2024_tract_out, target_counties,
                      "Saved 2024 tract-source counties", key = "tr2020_id")
print(rent_raw_qa_16, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(rent_raw_qa_2024_tract, n = Inf, width = Inf)
bind_rows(
  acs16_out |> transmute(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5), rent_value = rentE,
                         rent_measure = "native rentE", product = "2016_tract"),
  acs_2024_tract_out |>
    transmute(county = substr(tr2020_id, 3, 5), rent_value = rentE,
              rent_measure = "native rentE", product = "2024_tract")
) |>
  group_by(product, rent_measure, county) |>
  summarise(tracts = n(), missing_rent = sum(is.na(rent_value)),
            missing_share = mean(is.na(rent_value)), .groups = "drop") |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

## 4.6 Check inventory completeness and reconciliation

Missing inventory must agree exactly with `inventory_incomplete` by tract key.
Every complete inventory must be finite, nonnegative, and equal to the sum of
its three separately aggregated components. Zero-contributor targets must have
zero components and inventory. These checks apply whether or not a parity
reference exists or contains inventory; no partial total is accepted.

Report affected source IDs, missing components, target IDs, and county counts
for each product. Reconcile source-first and target-first inventory over
**complete targets only**. Each native tract has unit weight. Incomplete targets
are reported separately; complete-target totals do not estimate the entire sample.

```{r validate-rental-inventory-step2}
assert_rental_inventory(acs16_out, inventory_16, "Saved 2016 inventory")
assert_rental_inventory(acs_2024_tract_out, inventory_2024_tract,
                        "Saved 2024 tract-source inventory", key = "tr2020_id")
stopifnot(`Saving must preserve every 2016 value and row` = identical(acs16_out, acs_16), `Saving must preserve every 2024 tract-source value and row` = identical(acs_2024_tract_out,
    acs_2024_tract))
print(inventory_missing_sources_16, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(inventory_missing_sources_2024_tract, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(bind_rows(`2016_tract` = inventory_county_qa_16, `2024_tract` = inventory_county_qa_2024_tract,
    .id = "product"), n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(bind_rows(`2016_tract` = reconcile_rental_inventory(acs_16, inventory_16, tr2010_id), `2024_tract` = reconcile_rental_inventory(acs_2024_tract,
    inventory_2024_tract, tr2020_id), .id = "product"), n = Inf, width = Inf)
```
